correctness.rationale: Complete 945-source finite classification independently generated by an insertion bijection and exhaustive balanced-word enumeration. The exact lower witness has 33 pairwise disjoint descendant sets. The 105 nonnegative integer dual weights sum to 339636 with scale 10000 and satisfy every one of the 945 source covering inequalities. Therefore no code has 34 sources. The embedded checker reproduces all inequalities and returns VERIFY_OK; no partial enumeration is used.

originality.rationale: The full-text tree/Stirling sources establish a bijection and enumerators, not deletion-code capacity. Ordinary permutation deletion theorems concern a different source and erasure channel. The 2024 full open-access Stirling article treats deletion of the prescribed largest pair for structural purposes, not a zero-error unknown-pair deletion code. No checked source or exact table provides the 33 optimum. The 2014 multipermutation-deletion paper was accessible only at abstract level and is explicitly retained as a historical-priority risk.

value.rationale: Whole-label deletion naturally models contraction of any edge in an ordered recursive increasing tree. Correcting unknown edge contraction is a motivated zero-error coding task. The exact five-label maximum is not a textbook substitution from the odd-double-factorial enumeration or standard permutation-deletion constructions: the 33 lower witness and fractional upper witness together settle a new exact packing invariant. No generalization beyond order five is claimed.
